To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) evaluation is a crucial part of outlier detection research and that (ii) existing evaluation methods have to be extended to allow for a more detailed and meaningful comparison of different outlier detection methods.
(a) the evaluation of outlier detection methods should consider the class imbalance problem, and that (b) the similarity of two rankings can be evaluated using the Spearman correlation coefficient.

the evaluation of outlier detection methods should take into account the class imbalance problem, that the evaluation methods should allow for the comparison of the performance of different methods, that the evaluation results are highly sensitive to the outlier score ranking, and that the evaluation methods need to be adapted to the specific outlier score ranking used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the performance of existing outlier detection algorithms and their correlation with respect to their detection performance.
the evaluation of outlier detection methods, and in particular with the assessment of similarity between rankings of outlier scores.
the development and application of a new evaluation framework to outlier detection methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evaluation methods currently in use are insufficient to compare and assess the performance of existing outlier detection techniques and are not suitable to design ensembles of these techniques.
the evaluation framework we present is the most comprehensive and detailed evaluation framework to date.

our new evaluation framework provides the means for a more meaningful evaluation of outlier detection methods and for the construction of outlier detection ensembles.

a meaningful comparison of outlier detection methods is possible and can be done using a set of evaluation methods that are based on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for each class.
